07 / Solution approach
05 / Beyond development

Think beyond the build.

The decisions, engineering discipline, and operational ownership behind a successful enterprise solution.

01 · DECISION STUDIO

Choose the right approach.

CLOUD FLOW

When Cloud?

Use cloud flows for event-driven orchestration, approvals, connector-based integration, scheduled jobs, and supported APIs. Prefer this when the system exposes a stable connector or HTTP/API boundary.

Best fit: event triggers · approvals · integrations
POWER AUTOMATE DESKTOP

When PAD?

Use desktop flows when a required legacy application has no viable API or connector and the process must interact with its user interface. Plan machine availability, credentials, selectors, retries, monitoring, and attended/unattended licensing.

Best fit: legacy UI · repetitive desktop work
DATAVERSE

Why Dataverse?

Choose Dataverse when the solution needs relational business data, role-based security, business rules, auditing, structured relationships, and managed application lifecycle. Use SharePoint or another store when the requirements are simpler or document-centric.

Best fit: governed business records · relationships

10 / Delivery reality

Why projects fail before the code does.

The most expensive delivery problems often begin with unresolved requirements, scope, dependencies, and ownership—not with the technology itself.

THE DELIVERY TRAP

Uncertainty compounds.

  • Requirements remain ambiguous
  • Scope changes without impact review
  • Dependencies are discovered late
  • Rework compresses testing time
  • Quality and trust are put at risk
TURN RISK INTO READINESS →
THE READINESS RESPONSE

Make decisions visible.

  • Agree acceptance criteria early
  • Track assumptions and dependencies
  • Use change impact assessment
  • Protect test and release gates
  • Assign operational ownership
Agile delivery, Jira, client reviews, changing priorities, and delivery pressure are not inherently the problem. The risk is allowing critical uncertainty to remain unresolved while development is already moving.
11 / Architecture decision studio
09 / Architecture decision studio

Decisions before diagrams.

A compact view of how requirements, constraints, risk, and maintainability shape an enterprise solution—not a one-size-fits-all technology recipe.

Decision brief / orchestration

Choose the execution path deliberately.

Start with the process boundary, trigger, system interfaces, transaction volume, licensing, and operational ownership.

  • Cloud flow for supported connectors, events, approvals, and orchestration.
  • Desktop automation when a required interface has no viable supported integration.
  • API or custom connector when a governed interface is available and justified.
Decision brief / data foundation

Model the data for the operating model.

Evaluate relationships, security boundaries, validation, auditability, expected growth, and lifecycle management.

  • Dataverse where relational data, role-based access, and managed application lifecycle needs warrant it.
  • SharePoint for suitable document-centric or simpler list scenarios.
  • Document assumptions and trade-offs before committing to the platform.
12 / Technical decision studio

Trade-offs, made explicit.

The right choice depends on the use case, platform constraints, and operating model—not a one-size-fits-all rule.

DECISION / 01

Canvas or Model-driven?

Choose the experience based on task flow, data complexity, user needs, and maintenance expectations.

Canvas favors tailored task-focused interfaces. Model-driven apps suit data-centric processes built around Dataverse tables, forms, views, and role-based experiences.
DECISION / 02

SharePoint or Dataverse?

Compare relational complexity, security model, validation, scale, reporting, and ALM needs.

SharePoint can suit document-centric collaboration and simpler lists. Dataverse is designed for relational business data, richer security, structured logic, and model-driven application patterns.
DECISION / 03

Cloud flow or Desktop flow?

Use the most reliable supported integration path for the process boundary.

Prefer cloud flows for events, connectors, approvals, and APIs. Use desktop RPA when a required interface has no viable supported integration and UI automation is justified.

ROI SCORECARD · FOUR OUTCOMES

Business value trend after launch

One graph, four measurable signals. Each curve tracks how an outcome changes month by month.

ILLUSTRATIVE DATA
Time efficiency Cost impact User adoption Reliability
How to read this graph: The horizontal axis shows months after launch. The vertical axis is a relative score: 100 means the starting point; 120 means 20 index points above that starting point. A rising line means that outcome is improving. The score is not money or a percentage. Replace these illustrative lines with measured monthly results.

What each curve means

  • Time efficiencyMore work completed per unit of handling time, or less time per case.
  • Cost impactValidated operating-cost improvement after licensing, build, and support costs.
  • User adoptionIntended users actively using the app or solution.
  • ReliabilitySuccessful runs or completed transactions, with fewer failures and rework.
Important

Usage and reliability support the value story, but financial ROI must be calculated from validated benefits and total costs.

THE ROI CALCULATION

ROI (%) = (Net benefit ÷ Total cost) × 100

Net benefit = validated financial benefits − total solution cost.

Include the full costBuild and deliveryLicensing and connectorsSupport, training, and change
